subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should OpenClaw automatically remove or trim stale `.bak.*` and store-temp session artifacts during normal maintenance/startup, or should those remain recoverable except under explicit cleanup or disk-budget pressure?
rationale: Current code intentionally preserves `.bak.*` archives in normal retention, while the issue asks for broad automatic deletion of all stale session artifact classes; that is a product/data-retention decision before a new repair lane should change defaults.

options.title: Land a bounded cleanup contract
options.body: Keep this issue open, review the linked cleanup PRs, and require one policy-backed implementation that documents and tests deleted/reset, temp, and `.bak.*` behavior.

options.title: Preserve `.bak.*` by policy
options.body: Treat `.bak.*` as recovery evidence, update docs/cleanup output to make that explicit, and narrow this issue to stale deleted/reset/temp artifacts only.

options.title: Adopt proactive background sweeping
options.body: Approve startup/timer cleanup for stale artifacts and require upgrade-safe retention, dry-run reporting, and concurrency tests before merge.

recommendation.title: Land a bounded cleanup contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, review the linked cleanup PRs, and require one policy-backed implementation that documents and tests deleted/reset, temp, and `.bak.*` behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current session maintenance and cleanup contract that this decision would extend or constrain.
